audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read [Skill, Sion, Sion, Skill, Skill, Sion, Sion]; the packet reads [Skill, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai, Skill] and the mirrored maokai__sion audit has already moved to it.
audit.why: The content whys describe the packet chart exactly — 'Levels 1-3 are Maokai's window', 'he dictates every trade direction', whys[5] says your Heartsteel is 'not yet dominant', and whys[6] calls the late game 'a genuine skill matchup'. Only the tokens disagreed.
audit.corrected: Six rows flipped as matched full/content pairs: L2 through 1st item to Maokai, 2+ items to Skill. Level 1 already agreed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats saplings as constant zone spam and gives no cooldown for his ultimate.
audit.why: Sapling Toss is 18s at rank 1 and only falls to 14s — each one is a placed decision, not a blanket, which changes the advice from 'avoid the zone' to 'punish the 18 seconds after he throws'. Nature's Grasp is 130s at rank 1 with 3000 range, so the window after he spends it is nearly two minutes.
audit.corrected: Both cooldowns written into whys[3] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance is described only as an undodgeable lock-on root, and Sap Magic is described as saplings 'replenishing his HP'.
audit.why: Twisted Advance also makes him UNTARGETABLE while he travels (the brief's untargetable-dodges-burst flag) — so burst spent as he commits lands on nothing, and the answer is to wait it out rather than dump everything into it. It is a 14s cooldown at rank 1 from 525 range. And the healing is Sap Magic, his passive empowered attack, whose cooldown is reduced every time he casts a spell OR is struck by one — meaning Sion's own poke accelerates the enemy's healing, which is the opposite of what the page implies.
audit.corrected: Untargetability and the 14s cooldown stated in whys[1]; Sap Magic's real mechanic and its spell-driven acceleration stated in whys[3], late and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither of the two ultimate-level interactions in the brief appears on the page.
audit.why: The brief lists enemy-dash-deniable (your Unstoppable Onslaught answers Twisted Advance, so hold R for the engage rather than the poke) and terrain-cuts-retreat (Nature's Grasp can cut your retreat and you have no dash, so Flash is for the wall, not the damage). Both are decisions the player makes at level 6 and the page says nothing about either.

edits.before: His W root (Twisted Advance) locks on and cannot be dodged once activated — at level 2 it pins you inside saplings before your W-shield habit is reliable, giving him the short-trade advantage.
edits.after: Twisted Advance locks on from 525 and he is untargetable while it travels, so burst spent into it lands on nothing and you end up rooted — that is the whole short trade, on a 14s cooldown.

edits.before: The sapling zone control and knockback spam make charging Q nearly impossible without fog or a brush angle — Maokai comfortably out-pokes you from a distance with passive regen recovering any damage you deal.
edits.after: Sapling Toss is 18s at rank 1, so it is placement rather than spam — but Bramble Smash punts you out of a charge every 7s, and Sap Magic's cooldown drops each time he casts or is struck by a spell, so your poke feeds his regen.

edits.before: Stack his passive regeneration by sustaining through trades with saplings replenishing his HP between each skirmish
edits.after: Speed up Sap Magic by trading spells with you, so his empowered attack heals back everything your chip damage takes

edits.before: Levels 4-5 give him the full sapling-zone control toolkit and he can blanket the lane with slow-moving saplings that activate when you walk over them — play toward the caster-minion side of the lane where he has less brush to throw into. At 6 his R (Nature's Grasp) is a lane-width wave of roots that travels toward you; if you are trying to hold a charged Q and his R wave arrives, you WILL be rooted mid-channel, taking the full sapling burst. Trade only when his R is down or clearly not aimed at the lane — use that window to step up, force a W-shield trade, and back out.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 give him zone control, but Sapling Toss is 18s at rank 1 — each one is a placed decision, not a blanket, so punish the seconds after he throws and walk the caster side where he has less brush to aim at. At 6 Nature's Grasp is a 3000-range wall of roots on a 130s cooldown that advances at you; caught holding a charge, you eat the root and the follow-up. Trade while it is down. Save your own R for the engage rather than the poke — it answers Twisted Advance — and since you have no dash, keep Flash for his wall, not for the damage.

edits.before: Late game this resolves back into a genuine tank mirror — your zombie passive (Glory in Death) means even a losing fight costs him HP he cannot ignore, and your W-shield scales into a massive absorb on a full HP stack. The duel comes down to one thing: who lands their lockdown first. His W root sets up his entire combo; your charged Q stun sets up E-armor-shred and R follow-up. Respect his root, do not channel Q with his W available, and the matchup evens out at two items where your passive HP accumulation finally matches his sapling sustain.
edits.after: Late game this resolves back into a genuine tank mirror — your zombie passive (Glory in Death) means even a losing fight costs him HP he cannot ignore, and your W-shield scales into a massive absorb on a full HP stack. The duel comes down to who lands lockdown first, and to healing: Sap Magic's cooldown falls every time he casts a spell or is hit by one, so a long brawl without Grievous Wounds refunds him. Respect the root, do not start a charge with Twisted Advance up, and the matchup evens at two items where your HP accumulation matches his sustain.

notes: Chart was wrong on six rows in both layers while the prose already described the packet's version; flipped as matched pairs, which also puts this page back in agreement with the mirrored maokai__sion audit. The most useful new fact is that Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced when Maokai is STRUCK by a spell, not only when he casts one — so Sion poking with Roar of the Slayer actively accelerates the enemy's healing, which reframes both the poke pattern and the anti-heal timing. Twisted Advance's untargetability was also missing: burst dumped as he commits is wasted. I marked the two brief-supplied level-6 interactions (R denying his dash, his wall cutting retreat) as Medium confidence — they come from the repo's missing-interaction data rather than from anything in Riot's ability text, and neither kit states how a knockup interacts with a dash in flight. Full-layer strings carry mojibake em dashes; I made no full-layer prose edits here beyond the enum sides.
